correctness.rationale: The proof gives a complete face classification under girth>=6, a self-contained contractible tree base, a collision-free relative Morse matching when a chord is added, strict decreasing distance on all gradient paths, an exact b(H)+1 critical 3-cell count, null attaching maps to a 2-connected wedge, and integral Alexander-duality shift N-j-3=3. An independently replayable finite verifier checks exact face and matching claims for all 1356 six-vertex connected high-girth labeled graphs plus nine named examples, including the Heawood incidence graph. Finite checks are not used to prove the infinite statement. Risks: reliance on standard relative discrete Morse and integral Alexander duality, whose hypotheses are met.

value.rationale: The exact integral homology and entire dual homotopy type are classified for every connected graph of girth>=6, solely by the natural cyclomatic number b, with nontrivial quadratic multiplicity b(b+1)/2. Relative chord attachments explain structurally how topology accumulates, giving a torsion-free classification and broad nonshellability theorem. The previously published Heawood rank 36 is explained conceptually rather than recomputed as an isolated finite fact. The infinite class allows intersecting long cycles and arbitrary cycle rank, not an arbitrary slice.
